punchline: Moltke could not turn his plan around, because it had no second branch.
thirty_sec: On 1 August 1914 the Kaiser, misled by a telegram from London, wanted the whole army sent east; Moltke said it could not be done, though an eastern deployment plan had existed and he had set it aside in 1913.
question: Which plan you are proudest of has no second route anyone has walked through?
key_contrast: A one-branch plan treats even good news as a threat.
